dataPoints.note: Inflation rate 2024 — context for fuel/energy relief
Inflation rate 2023 — high energy costs drove FiU48

commentary: Sweden's supplementary budget (HD01FiU48) cuts fuel taxes by 82 ore/liter for petrol and 319 SEK/m3 for diesel from May through September 2026 — reducing both to the EU energy tax directive minimum. This 4.1 billion SEK intervention comes as Sweden's GDP growth recovered to 0.82% in 2024 after a -0.20% contraction in 2023, but Swedish inflation peaked at 8.5% in 2023 before falling to 1.8% in 2024 — meaning household energy costs remain a live political issue even as headline inflation normalised. With approximately 5.7 million Swedish drivers and petrol at approximately 17 SEK/liter in spring 2026, the 82-ore cut provides a 5% pump-price reduction visible to every driver before the September 14 election. The Nordic comparison underscores the stakes: Denmark grew at 1.75% in 2024 versus Sweden's 0.82%, giving the opposition evidence that Sweden's structural recovery lags neighbours — which the government answers with direct household relief.
